en.headline: WWII British mortar fuze detonated on North Point hillside
en.dek: Police Explosive Ordnance Disposal officers destroyed the device on the slope opposite Braemar Hill Mansions at 1.18pm; no injuries and no evacuation required.
body: A World War II British mortar fuze found on a hillside in North Point was safely detonated by police on Tuesday afternoon, with no injuries and no need to evacuate residents.

Police received a report at about 10.57am that a suspected bomb had been found on the slope opposite Block 11 of Braemar Hill Mansions on Braemar Hill Road. Officers confirmed the object was a British mortar fuze about 7cm long and 4cm in diameter. Fire Services deployed a robot on standby while the scene was cordoned.
Explosive Ordnance Disposal officers detonated the device in place at 1.18pm. Authorities said the location on open ground allowed a controlled blast without clearing the estate or surrounding area.

zh.headline: 北角山邊發現二戰英式迫擊砲彈引信 警方即場引爆
zh.dek: 爆炸品處理課人員下午1時18分在寶馬山道賽西湖大廈對開山邊安全引爆，無人受傷亦毋須疏散。
body: 北角寶馬山道賽西湖大廈11座對開山邊周二發現一枚二戰時期英式迫擊砲彈引信，警方爆炸品處理課人員於下午1時18分即場引爆，事件中無人受傷及毋須疏散。
警方上午約10時57分接報，指該處山邊發現懷疑炸彈。人員到場後確認為長約7厘米、直徑約4厘米的英式迫擊砲彈引信，隨即封鎖現場，消防亦出動機械人戒備。
爆炸品處理課人員其後到場，於下午1時18分將引信即場引爆。當局表示位置屬開放山邊，毋須疏散屋苑或附近居民。
